items.title: This Is the Dev Setup You’re Looking For: My Journey to Chromebook Development (The Dad Edition)
items.description: The Preamble: When Life (and a Baby) Confined My Workspace Let’s be real. For as long as I can remember in this game, my setup was all about raw power . My rig? A high-spec desktop and a 15" ASUS ROG that sounded like a jet engine when the fans kicked in. That ROG was my own personal Death Star — insane firepower, but the battery life? Let’s just say it had a “thermal exhaust port” vulnerability.

items.title: Rendering React on Golang with V8Go
items.description: Server-side rendering (SSR) is essential for improving web performance, SEO, and initial page load experience. React provides built-in SSR capabilities through react-dom/server, but this typically requires a Node.js environment. What if we want to run and render React components without Node.js?

items.title: Parsing TAR files with Plain JavaScript
items.description: In the world of web development, there’s often a need to handle various file formats directly in the browser. One such format is TAR (Tape Archive), commonly used for packaging multiple files and directories into a single file. This article demystifies TAR files and gives a practical guide to parsing them with plain JavaScript in the browser.

items.title: Why did I remove every Javascript build step on my website
items.description: In the ever-evolving world of web development, it’s easy to get caught up in the latest trends and tools. But sometimes, taking a step back and simplifying can lead to surprising benefits. This is my journey of stripping away every JavaScript build step from my website and returning to the basics of pure JavaScript and HTML.
